title: Bidirectional A* in Outram: Fastest Routes!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* carve through a street-map graph in Outram, shrinking the search from both ends at once. The visualization highlights how two A* frontiers meet efficiently for shorter paths with fewer expansions.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ Bidirectional A* in Singapore (Outram)! We’re not just searching from start → goal—we do it from both sides.

🔍 Here’s the deep idea: Bidirectional A* runs two simultaneous A* searches—one forward from the origin and one backward from the destination—using consistent heuristics to keep the cost estimates “admissible enough” for optimality on the grid/road graph. When the two frontiers intersect, we stitch the partial paths into a complete route, dramatically cutting the explored space.

🗺️ Real street maps become a weighted graph: intersections are nodes, roads are edges, and edge weights can represent travel time/distance. That means graph search is doing the heavy lifting—prioritizing low estimated total cost (g + h) while avoiding unnecessary detours.

🔥 Want to see how your city’s streets behave as a graph? Comment your neighborhood and I’ll generate the next visualization. ❤️ Follow for more algorithm-to-real-world map demos!
fb_caption:
🚗💡 Bidirectional A* makes route-finding feel “smarter” by searching from both the start and the destination at the same time. In a graph built from real street maps (nodes = intersections, edges = roads with weights), this reduces expansions and finds efficient paths faster when compared to a single-ended search.
